# Results

## Regeneration under varying overstory retention

The thesis results provide the starting material for basal area, understory
density, and sprout-height summaries. At 10 years after harvest, redwood
regeneration was greatest in the most open treatment and declined with greater
overstory retention. Tanoak responses were comparatively modest. Redwood and
tanoak sprout-height findings will remain in the main results; other species
will be retained as descriptive context where useful rather than as dedicated
main-text analyses. The final figures and summaries will retain these results
only after the publication presentation and modeling review are complete.

## Fuel conditions as reference values

Fuel conditions are reported second to support interpretation of the
silvicultural treatments and to characterize the management-relevant transition
before and after precommercial thinning. The thesis found comparatively few
treatment differences in fine dead fuels before precommercial thinning, whereas
vegetation fuels were greater in more open treatments. The publication analysis
will separate fuel components that were previously combined, report phase-
specific estimates and uncertainty, and evaluate the PCT-associated contrast.
Treatment comparisons will be retained where they clarify PCT or retained-
overstory implications.
